subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should OpenClaw bound Docker sandbox prep with a default fail-fast timeout, and should that deadline cover prune, config-hash inspection, container create/start, and setup behavior?
rationale: The bug is real at source level, but timeout defaults and fail-soft behavior can intentionally change slow Docker setups from long waits into sandbox unavailability errors.

options.title: Refresh the full timeout path
options.body: Refresh or replace the linked PR so the deadline covers the Docker control-plane prep path, preserves current sandbox workspace behavior, documents the config/default, and includes real wedged-Docker proof.

options.title: Land a narrow mitigation
options.body: Accept a smaller Docker exec/init deadline while explicitly tracking prune/hash and broader OrbStack cold-start gaps as follow-up work.

options.title: Hold for live repro first
options.body: Wait for the reporter or maintainer to attach logs or run a macOS/OrbStack reproduction before choosing timeout semantics.

recommendation.title: Refresh the full timeout path
